correctness.rationale: The coordinatewise equation \(x_i^2+x_i=S\) is exact. In odd characteristic, the full solution set is partitioned into one exceptional scalar point and equivalence classes of sign vectors and nonzero roots of the displayed quadratic; the latter classes have size exactly two. The discriminant root count gives all branches. In characteristic two, Artin–Schreier roots and a two-to-one complement identification give every case. All candidate root equations have coefficients in the prime field and degree at most two, proving quadratic splitting and parity dependence. Standalone direct finite-field brute force agreed in 38 configurations, with no infinite claim inferred from enumeration.

originality.rationale: The complete-graph algebra and its graph-theoretic expansion were already introduced in arXiv:2605.12672, but the exact idempotent-census formulas, universal quadratic splitting over the prime field, and extension-parity law were not stated in its complete-graph example or relevant results. arXiv:2610.22248 proves a general geometric \(2^n\) upper bound and an average count over all perfect structure matrices, which do not imply a fixed complete-graph count. The nearest indexed results concern other evolution-algebra families; residual unindexed equivalence risk remains.
residual_risks: Equivalent idempotent-census calculations may exist in older, non-indexed, or differently named work.
The graph-specific result does not address weighted complete graphs or general finite-field expander evolution algebras.
The later October 2026 survey supplies a general upper bound; claiming that bound alone as new would be invalid, so the distinct arithmetic formulas are the novelty claim.

value.rationale: Idempotents are equilibrium points of the squaring evolution map. An exact, all-dimensional census for the canonical complete-graph algebra, including field-of-definition degree, sharp geometric maximum in almost all odd characteristics, and explicit exceptional deficits, identifies a mathematically natural arithmetic invariant absent from the motivating expansion treatment. The result is a complete family theorem, not an arbitrary finite slice or routine recomputation of an existing table.
